builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models
summary: MoMoVL replaces uniform-precision or modality-agnostic mixed-precision quantization of MoE-based VLMs with a bit-width assignment driven by per-expert activation profiles and per-modality (vision vs. text) quantization sensitivity. The cost is a modest accuracy drop relative to the uniform-precision baseline and the added complexity of computing modality-aware, per-expert bit allocations during compression. It can fail if the target model is not a sparsely-activated MoE VLM, if the expert-importance statistics do not transfer across workloads, or if the modest accuracy loss is unacceptable for the deployment task.
rationale: The method targets on-device MoE-based VLM inference, which is outside the reader's stated infrastructure of a single 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs, so it is only relevant if they later adopt sparsely-activated VLMs under tight memory budgets.
technique: Modality-aware mixed-precision quantization of MoE VLMs

claims.statement: MoMoVL replaces uniform-precision or modality-agnostic mixed-precision quantization of MoE-based VLMs with a bit-width assignment driven by per-expert activation profiles and per-modality (vision vs. text) quantization sensitivity. The cost is a modest accuracy drop relative to the uniform-precision baseline and the added complexity of computing modality-aware, per-expert bit allocations during compression. It can fail if the target model is not a sparsely-activated MoE VLM, if the expert-importance statistics do not transfer across workloads, or if the modest accuracy loss is unacceptable for the deployment task.

Reduces memory footprint by up to 15.44% relative to a uniform-precision baseline, with a modest accuracy drop, and improves the accuracy-compression trade-off over state-of-the-art mixed-precision baselines.
